injuryReports.returnComment: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.

injuryReports.name: DJ Uiagalelei
injuryReports.returnComment: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.
injuryReports.injury: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Quentin Johnston
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.
injuryReports.injury: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Keaton Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Omarion Hampton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Derius Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.
injuryReports.injury: Davis caught one of two targets for a 15-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Cam Hart
injuryReports.returnComment: Hart exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. Rodney Shelley will play outside cornerback opposite Donte Jackson while Hart undergoes further evaluation.
injuryReports.injury: Hart (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Isas Waxter
injuryReports.returnComment: The special-teamer will not return to Sunday's contest after exiting in the first quarter. A number of players could step up to contribute on special teams in Waxter's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Justin Eboigbe
injuryReports.returnComment: Eboigbe was hurt in the first quarter, and his return is uncertain. Nick Barrett will likely pick up more defensive snaps for as long as Eboigbe remains sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Denzel Perryman
injuryReports.returnComment: Perryman logged a pair of limited sessions during Week 9 prep but is not quite ready to return to the Chargers' 53-man roster. The inside linebacker will continue his recovery during Week 10 prep in the hopes of making his 2026 regular-season debut soon.
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: David Njoku
injuryReports.returnComment: Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Rodney Shelley
injuryReports.returnComment: Shelley missed each of Los Angeles' past three games while tending to an ankle injury. However, he followed two limited practices to begin this week with a full session Friday to position himself for a return Sunday. Shelley has played a rotational role in the secondary when active this season while also contributing on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Shelley (ankle) has no designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Donte Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson missed each of the Chargers' past three games due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to log a full practice session Friday and is set to return to action versus Houston. Before getting hurt, he started in three of his four appearances to begin the season, so he'll likely return to that role Sunday, especially since fellow cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out.
injuryReports.injury: Jackson (hamstring) does not have a designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Whittington
injuryReports.returnComment: ir
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Puka Nacua
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Trent McDuffie
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Joe Cardona
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Terrance Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Colby Parkinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles in receptions, though he didn't turn them into many yards. Still, it was his third straight contest with at least four catches, so Parkinson looks to be developing into a favorite target of QB Matthew Stafford. That could come in handy in Week 10 and beyond, as Stafford is going to need to turn to other pass catchers to help make up for the massive production being lost in the absence of Puka Nacua, who is expected to land on IR due to knee and turf-toe injuries.
injuryReports.injury: Parkinson notched four catches for 13 yards on four targets in a 20-13 win over Washington on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Brandon McManus
injuryReports.returnComment: McManus' field goals were good from 33 and 20 yards, and he's now made all 13 of his kicks through three games with Los Angeles. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) now out for the foreseeable future, this offense figures to struggle to score points, downgrading McManus in the fantasy kicker rankings.
injuryReports.injury: McManus made both of his field-goal tries and both PATs in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Steve Avila
injuryReports.returnComment: McVay said part of the decision whether to place Avila on IR will be influenced by concerns that the team could use up all of its eight injured-reserve slots for players eligible to return later in the season. Either way, for as long as Avila remains sidelined, 2024 sixth rounder Beaux Limmer projects to fill in at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Myles Garrett
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his return from a knee injury that had sidelined him since Week 1, Garrett made an immediate impact and accounted for three of the Rams' four sacks of Jayden Daniels on the afternoon, with Braden Fiske and Shaun Dolac splitting the other. A healthy Garrett's presence in the front seven changes the entire complexion of the defense, and he could continue to make up for lost time in Week 10 against Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals.
injuryReports.injury: Garrett recorded 3.0 sacks and forced a fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Blake Corum
injuryReports.returnComment: The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.
injuryReports.injury: Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Matthew Stafford
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.
injuryReports.injury: Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry.

injuryReports.name: Kyren Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.
injuryReports.injury: Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington.

injuryReports.name: Grant Stuard
injuryReports.returnComment: Stuard finished the week as a limited participant in Friday's practice due to a hamstring injury that occurred during Week 8 warmups. The 28-year-old has played in all eight Rams games this season, recording two total tackles (one solo).
injuryReports.injury: Stuard is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Kam Curl
injuryReports.returnComment: Curl is set to suit up for Sunday's game despite missing the Rams' Wednesday and Thursday practice sessions. The strong safety will need to anchor the team's secondary due to the absence of starting cornerbacks Jaylen Watson (shoulder, IR) and Trent McDuffie (back).
injuryReports.injury: Curl (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson exited Sunday's win over the Chargers early with a severe shoulder injury. The cornerback will undergo surgery while on IR, which will end his season. Watson ends the season with 24 tackles (14 solo) and nine passes defensed, including one interception, over seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Ronnie Rivers
injuryReports.returnComment: Rivers missed six games while on injured reserve with a calf injury he sustained in the Rams' Week 2 loss to the Giants. The 27-year-old has returned ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders and has no injury designation headed into the contest. Rivers will likely be a special-teams contributor with no real role in the Rams' offense.
injuryReports.injury: The Rams activated Rivers (calf) from injured reserve Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Quentin Lake
injuryReports.returnComment: Lake was able to secure exactly seven takedowns for the third straight week, as he has now registered six or more tackles in every game this season. The 27-year-old's biggest moment of the contest came in the first quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert for his third interception of the year. Lake has now compiled 56 total tackles (34 solo), a forced fumble, and 11 passes defensed, three of which are interceptions, over eight games so far in the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Lake recorded seven total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Karty
injuryReports.returnComment: Karty was elevated from the practice squad for each of the Rams' previous two games and handled kickoff duties while Brandon McManus kicked field goals and extra points. That arrangement isn't expected to change moving forward, per Nate Adkins of The Athletic, so it would likely take a McManus slump or injury for Karty to get a shot at the fantasy-relevant aspects of the kicker position.
injuryReports.injury: The Rams signed Karty to their active roster Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Higbee
injuryReports.returnComment: Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).
injuryReports.injury: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory.

injuryReports.name: Dean Connors
injuryReports.returnComment: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Hand

injuryReports.name: Kyle McCord
injuryReports.returnComment: A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: McCord will step in as the Dolphins' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Indianapolis after Miami placed Malik Willis (core) on injured reserve Tuesday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Malik Willis
injuryReports.returnComment: ir
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Zach Sieler
injuryReports.returnComment: Sieler reportedly sustained the injury on the Dolphins' first defensive play of the game and proceeded to play with the ruptured biceps throughout the contest. The standout defensive lineman will likely undergo surgery in the coming days and will face a projected 5-to-6-month recovery timeline, which could limit his availability for OTAs in the spring. The 31-year-old Sieler finishes the 2026 campaign with 24 tackles (14 solo) and 2.0 sacks over his eight appearances with Miami.
injuryReports.injury: Biceps

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Zane Gonzalez
injuryReports.returnComment: Miami now has used the maximum three standard elevations on Gonzalez, and he's made just five of seven field-goal attempts and all five PATs across three games. The Dolphins will need to sign the kicker to the active roster if he's going to keep kicking for the team moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Gonzalez reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Kaytron Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen's catch came on a fake punt, so it was an outlier of a play. He played just six offensive snaps behind clear RB1 Ollie Gordon. Since joining Miami via waivers last month, Allen has logged 31 snaps on special teams and six on offense. He has no fantasy appeal.
injuryReports.injury: Allen caught a 46-yard pass in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for minus-1 yard.

injuryReports.name: Greg Dulcich
injuryReports.returnComment: Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.
injuryReports.injury: Dulcich caught two of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Malik Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Douglas
injuryReports.returnComment: Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.
injuryReports.injury: Douglas secured six of eight targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ollie Gordon II
injuryReports.returnComment: Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Will Kacmarek
injuryReports.returnComment: Kacmarek took a low hit after making a catch in the third quarter and subsequently went to the medical tent. He then returned to the sideline and tested out the injured leg, so he appears to be at least attempting to re-enter the contest. If Kacmarek can't return, however, Greg Dulcich and Seydou Traore will be Miami's two healthy active tight ends.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Malik Herring
injuryReports.returnComment: Herring suffered a neck injury in the Week 8 loss to New England. Despite logging three limited practices throughout the week and being listed as questionable, he's good to go for the meeting with Detroit. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games in 2026, accruing nine total tackles (four solo) and 1.0 sacks.
injuryReports.injury: Herring (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Kadyn Proctor
injuryReports.returnComment: Proctor suffered a concussion in Week 7 against the Jets and didn't play this past Sunday versus New England. However, he was a full participant in all three of Miami's practices this week and has cleared concussion protocol. Proctor is therefore set to reclaim his starting role at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Proctor (concussion) does not have a designation for Sunday's Week 9 matchup versus Detroit, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Rodriguez
injuryReports.returnComment: Rodriguez fell three tackles shy of Jordyn Brooks' team-leading total as the Dolphins dropped to 1-6. The rookie second-round pick's 12 tackles over the past two games mark the most fallow two-game stretch of Rodriguez's young career in that category. He'll try to pick up the pace in Week 9 against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Rodriguez notched eight tackles (two solo) and forced a fumble in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks led the Dolphins in tackles during the loss, which dropped Miami's record to 1-6. The 29-year-old linebacker has slowed down a bit after leading the NFL with 183 tackles (99 solo) during the 2025 regular season, though he's still averaging a respectable nine tackles per game in 2026. He could draw interest on the trade market from contending teams in search of help at linebacker.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks recorded 11 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Max Brosmer
injuryReports.returnComment: Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.
injuryReports.injury: Brosmer completed six of seven attempts for 58 yards in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Odell Beckham Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Signed off the practice squad ahead of Monday's game against the Bills, Beckham made his Vikings debut in the 23-6 loss, going without a target while playing just two snaps on offense. He'll end up giving up his spot on the 53-man roster just one day later after the Vikings brought in quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders prior to the deadline, but Beckham won't be without a home for long. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Beckham is expected to re-sign with the Vikings' practice squad and will be eligible to be elevated for three games.
injuryReports.injury: The Vikings released Beckham on Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Kyler Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jauan Jennings
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Jordan Addison
injuryReports.returnComment: Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.
injuryReports.injury: Addison secured two of three targets for 28 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Mason
injuryReports.returnComment: Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: T.J. Hockenson
injuryReports.returnComment: In addition to leading the Vikings in receptions, Hockenson finished second in receiving yardage and targets in a rough performance by Minnesota's offense. The veteran wideout has hauled in exactly four catches in four straight games, though he snapped a two-game TD streak Monday. It remains to be seen who will be throwing passes for Minnesota next Sunday in Green Bay, as Carson Wentz struggled enormously Monday and Kyler Murray currently is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
injuryReports.injury: Hockenson recorded four catches for 33 yards on seven targets in a loss to Buffalo on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Carson Wentz
injuryReports.returnComment: Wentz had typically put together competent performances in his opportunities to lead head coach Kevin O'Connell's offense in the past, but Monday night was a clear exception. Wentz took only one sack, but he banged up his right hand on a first-half pass attempt, then had his foot stepped on by offensive lineman Joe Huber in the second half, the latter of which required a visit to the medical tent. Wentz also repeatedly failed to master what had been a vulnerable Bills pass defense, averaging a minuscule 3.2 yards per attempt. He tossed interceptions on back-to-back drives to open the second half as well, and although they only led to one field goal for Buffalo, they were indicative of the kind of night it was for the veteran signal-caller. Wentz ultimately was pulled for Max Brosmer for the Vikings' final drive, and if Murray can't suit up for a Week 10 road showdown with the Packers on Sunday, it remains to be seen if Wentz will get another crack at a starting assignment.
injuryReports.injury: Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed once for no gain in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Justin Jefferson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jefferson led the Vikings in receiving yards and targets, but the insertion of Carson Wentz at quarterback in place of Kyler Murray (hamstring) led to a very inefficient night for the star receiver. Jefferson's final catch of the night, which went for a 19-yard gain, came on a pass from Max Brosmer, so Jefferson secured just two of the 10 targets that an ineffective Wentz sent his way. Jefferson has been having a generally quiet season even when working with Murray -- he doesn't have any 100-yard games and has posted Monday night's yardage total or less in five of seven games -- but his outlook would be brighter if Murray can return for Sunday's Week 10 road showdown against the Packers.
injuryReports.injury: Jefferson brought in three of 11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Kyle Van Noy
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Van Noy (calf) has returned to Monday night's matchup with Buffalo, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Demond Claiborne
injuryReports.returnComment: ir
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Theo Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson did not practice Thursday and Friday. While he practiced in a limited capacity Saturday, it still wasn't enough to avoid a questionable designation. However, Jackson has since been upgraded and is ready to go versus the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Jackson (quadriceps) is active for Monday's game against Buffalo, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.
injuryReports.injury: Van Ginkel (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's matchup against the Bills, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Christian Darrisaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Darrisaw began Week 9 prep with a limited session Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday. As such, he should be good to go for Monday's matchup against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Darrisaw (shoulder) was a full practice participant Friday.

injuryReports.name: DeeJay Dallas
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas will return to the active roster after playing in the first five contests of the year with the Vikings before being released and ultimately returning to the team as a member of the practice squad in late October. The running back has rushed four times for 14 yards and caught all four of his targets for 34 yards over seven contests with Minnesota this year, and he figures to operate in an extreme depth role behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason on Monday night versus Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Dallas was signed to the Vikings' active roster Wednesday, Craig Peters of the team's official website reports.

injuryReports.name: Eric Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson finished second on the Vikings in stops, behind only Josh Metellus (13). One of his tackles was a sack of Jared Goff for a 10-yard loss on Detroit's first drive of the game, resulting in a Detroit punt. Wilson has 3.0 sacks through seven games, so he could surpass the career-best mark of 6.5 sacks he recorded over 17 regular-season games last year.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson registered 11 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's loss to Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Metellus
injuryReports.returnComment: Metellus led Minnesota in tackles and recorded a season-high mark in the process. He's been a consistent presence for the Vikings' tough defense this season, playing every defensive snap in six of the team's seven contests so far. Metellus is up to 50 stops through seven games, putting him on pace for the third triple-digit tackle campaign of his career.
injuryReports.injury: Metellus recorded 13 tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass in a Week 8 defeat against Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Charles Woods
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: TreVeyon Henderson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: A.J. Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Andy Borregales
injuryReports.returnComment: Borregales didn't attempt a field goal, and it was the second time this season that he didn't kick any. For the year, the second-year kicker in 10 of 13 on FGAs and has made 23 of 24 extra points. He'll be a fantasy target for next Sunday's potential shootout in Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Borregales made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Ben Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Corey Kiner
injuryReports.returnComment: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.
injuryReports.injury: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: DeMario Douglas
injuryReports.returnComment: Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Drake Maye
injuryReports.returnComment: Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions while adding one rush for three yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Mack Hollins
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.
injuryReports.injury: Hollins caught three of six targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Patriots.

injuryReports.name: Efton Chism III
injuryReports.returnComment: Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Chism caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Henry returned to action after suffering a foot injury in the first half of the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins and missing the majority of that contest. The tight end was held in check versus Green Bay, finishing with three or fewer catches for the sixth time this season. Henry has now reeled in 32 of 37 targets for 361 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Henry caught all three of his targets for 35 yards during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Brenden Schooler
injuryReports.returnComment: Strictly a special-teamer for New England, Schooler entered play Sunday with four tackles (two solo) across four games this season. His next chance to play will be next Sunday in Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Will Campbell
injuryReports.returnComment: Campbell suffered a knee injury in the second half, and he seems unlikely to be able to return before the conclusion of the team's Week 9 contest. In his absence, Caleb Lomu has taken over at left tackle versus Green Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Carlton Davis III
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis is in danger of missing the remainder of the game after suffering a knee injury in the second half. Channing Canada and Karon Prunty could be in line for an uptick in playing time if Davis is unable to return to the matchup.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Greg Van Roten
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Roten was placed on IR due to a hamstring issue in late September before being designated to return Wednesday. He was limited in all three practices this week, and New England has elected to hold him out of gameday action for at least another week. Van Roten's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Gabe Jacas
injuryReports.returnComment: Jacas made an early exit last Sunday versus Miami due to a knee issue. He was limited in the first two Patriots practices this week but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday, clearing the way for him to suit up in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Jacas (knee) does not have a designation for Sunday's contest versus Green Bay.

injuryReports.name: Marcus Bryant
injuryReports.returnComment: Bryant will return to action in Week 9 after spending the entirety of the regular season to this point on IR after suffering an ankle injury during the preseason. The 24-year-old will operate as a top reserve option behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses at offensive tackle moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Bryant (ankle) was activated from injured reserve by the Patriots on Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore noted that the Saints are still in the process of  "using the time allotted" to let Etienne workout with the training staff before designating him for return from injured reserve and opening his 21-day practice window. Though the 27-year-old back hasn't played since the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders, he's still just 34 yards behind quarterback Tyler Shough for the team lead in rushing yardage (162). Whether he's activated for Week 10 or at some point thereafter, Etienne's eventual return will provide a boost to a New Orleans running game that has struggled mightily through the midway point of the season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Stone Smartt
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: Erik McCoy
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Biceps

injuryReports.name: CJ Donaldson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Charlie Smyth
injuryReports.returnComment: Smyth was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 9 overtime win over Cleveland. He served as New Orleans' kicker in the contest and went 3-for-4 on FGAs while making both of his PAT attempts. That performance was likely good enough for Smyth to be elevated again for this Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: The Saints reverted Smyth to their practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Noah Fant
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end logged 47 percent of the offensive snaps but is mainly a blocker, while Juwan Johnson handles most of the pass-catching duties at the position. Fant has four catches for 30 yards over his last four games and is not even remotely on the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Fant caught one pass for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Devaughn Vele
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Alvin Kamara
injuryReports.returnComment: Kamara operated as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind Audric Estime (15-72-1) in Week 9. Estime was claimed off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday, and he immediately supplanted Kamara as the team's lead back. Kamara has yet to exceed 40 rushing yards in a game this season, and he has scored just one touchdown over the team's last four contests combined.
injuryReports.injury: Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards while catching three of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Juwan Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Tyson
injuryReports.returnComment: It wasn't the most dynamic performance from the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but it was just good to see Tyson on the field after he missed the first seven games of the season due to hamstring trouble, even if his longest gain went for just nine yards. Tyson's role in the offense figures to grow quickly if he can stay healthy, and he has the talent to put together a productive second half as the No. 2 option behind Chris Olave for quarterback Tyler Shough.
injuryReports.injury: Tyson caught four of five targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Audric Estime
injuryReports.returnComment: Claimed off waivers by New Orleans earlier in the week to add some depth to a depleted backfield, Estime ended up going up against his former Browns squad in his first game since rejoining the Saints. Since he had played for the Saints in 2025 and didn't need to learn head coach Kellen Moore's playbook, Estime was in prime position to step into a big role right away and capitalized on the opportunity, leading the backfield with 16 touches ahead of Alvin Kamara's nine. Estime capped his big performance with a two-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. While he certainly made a case for a consistent role in the offense, rookie CJ Donaldson (shoulder) could be back next week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) might be close to returning from injured reserve. Estime could still be atop the depth chart, at least temporarily, for a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Estime carried the ball 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also caught his only target for five yards.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Shough
injuryReports.returnComment: New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Chris Olave
injuryReports.returnComment: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards once again, but Juwan Johnson was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD of the day. Olave is the clear top option in the New Orleans passing attack, but with Jordyn Tyson finally making his pro debut Sunday, secondaries may have someone else to worry about in the second half of the season. Olave will take a 56-734-2 line on 83 targets into a Week 10 battle against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Olave caught seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Kelvin Banks Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Saints activated Banks from injured reserve Saturday. The starting left tackle was placed on IR in early September and had a 10-week return timeline, something the 22-year-old surpassed by a large margin. Banks is all set to suit up and protect quarterback Tyler Shough in Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Banks (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Martin Emerson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Emerson didn't participate in Friday's practice after kicking off the week limited Wednesday and Thursday. He appears to be ready to go, as he's not on the Saints' list of inactive players. The 26-year-old has 18 total tackles (16 solo), four pass deflections and two interceptions in six games.
injuryReports.injury: Emerson is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Justin Reid
injuryReports.returnComment: Reid was a full participant in all three Week 9 practice sessions. The Saints' starting strong safety has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Reid (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Cesar Ruiz
injuryReports.returnComment: Ruiz missed the Saints' pre-bye game against the Steelers in Paris, but the two weeks off were apparently enough to get him ready for Week 9 against Cleveland.
injuryReports.injury: Ruiz (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Nathan Shepherd
injuryReports.returnComment: Shepherd hasn't played since Week 4 but appears ready to return for Sunday's game against the Browns. He has 12 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, across 175 defensive snaps this season.
injuryReports.injury: Shepherd (illness) practiced in full Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Mooney
injuryReports.returnComment: Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.
injuryReports.injury: Mooney (chest) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Colton Hood
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Finger

injuryReports.name: J.J. McCarthy
injuryReports.returnComment: McCarthy was sidelined for most of the third quarter of this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles after sustaining a painful hip pointer, but he was able to finish out the game. Head coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence afterward that the injury wouldn't be anything that jeopardized McCarthy's status for Thursday's game against the Commanders, and the quarterback's ability to take every rep Tuesday clears the way for him to start on a short week. Through two starts and two appearances off the bench with the Giants, McCarthy has completed 43 of 68 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 622 yards (9.1 YPA), one touchdown and one interception to go with 51 yards on nine carries.
injuryReports.injury: McCarthy (hip) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Cam Skattebo
injuryReports.returnComment: Prior to Tuesday's practice, Skattebo told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the hamstring tear he sustained in a Week 7 overtime win over the Texans "wasn't too bad" and wouldn't prevent him from playing Thursday against the Commanders. With Skattebo proceeding to take every rep during Tuesday's session, he's now officially in the clear to step back into a lead role out of the New York backfield in Week 10. As a result of Skattebo's return to the lineup following a one-game absence, Devin Singletary -- who handled a season-high 23 touches in the Week 9 win over the Eagles -- is expected to see his opportunities get scaled back significantly.
injuryReports.injury: Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Fields
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie wideout is a distant third in the pecking order for targets behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely in the New York offense. For the season, Fields has 19 catches for 288 yards and one touchdown on 35 targets, averaging 36.0 yards per game across eight contests.
injuryReports.injury: Fields caught three of five targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Malik Harrison
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Abdul Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Dominic Zvada
injuryReports.returnComment: After Zvada missed both of his field-goal tries in the Giants' pre-Week 8 bye overtime win over the Texans two weeks ago, coach John Harbaugh stuck with the rookie kicker, and Zvada answered with a perfect afternoon against Philly. Zvada accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, converting field goals from 53, 49, 38 and 49 yards. On the season, he's 17-for-22 on field-goal tries and 13-for-13 on PATs.
injuryReports.injury: Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Likely
injuryReports.returnComment: Likely finished two targets shy of Malik Nabers' team-leading total and one receiving yard shy of Darnell Mooney's team-best mark, but the TE scored the Giants' lone touchdown of the game. That TD came on a five-yard pass in the third quarter from Jameis Winston, who replaced J.J. McCarthy (hip) for a drive and change before McCarthy returned to the game. Whether it's Winston or McCarthy under center, Likely projects to remain a key cog in the Giants' passing game for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, whose defense Likely carved up for 11 catches, 94 yards and two TDs in their Week 5 tie.
injuryReports.injury: Likely caught five of six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Devin Singletary
injuryReports.returnComment: Singletary blew by his previous season high of six carries, as fellow running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy were both sidelined by hamstring injuries. Skattebo has a chance to return for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, while Tracy won't be back prior to Week 12, so Singletary is likely to maintain an elevated role unless the Giants trade for another running back prior to Tuesday's deadline. Singletary didn't make the most of his added opportunities against the Eagles, averaging a meager 1.5 yards per carry.
injuryReports.injury: Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards and caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Malik Nabers
injuryReports.returnComment: Nabers recorded at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye but failed to extend that streak in Sunday's low-scoring win, during which J.J. McCarthy (hip) and Jameis Winston combined to throw for just 198 yards. The star wide receiver led the team with eight targets but finished third in receiving yards behind Darnell Mooney (54) and Isaiah Likely (53). Nabers had his hands on what would have been a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter but failed to secure a diving catch attempt. McCarthy left in the third quarter but managed to return later in the second half, and he can be tentatively penciled in as the starting QB for Thursday's home game against the leaky Commanders pass defense.
injuryReports.injury: Nabers caught five of eight targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Jalin Hyatt
injuryReports.returnComment: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.
injuryReports.injury: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: A lingering groin issue held Thomas to limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday to avoid a designation heading into the weekend. The star left tackle will therefore continue to anchor the offensive line for the first place Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas (groin) does not have a designation for Sunday's matchup in Philadelphia.

injuryReports.name: Greg Desrosiers Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Desrosiers is listed as running back No. 3 on the Giants' depth chart and could be in line to back up Devin Singletary on Sunday if Cam Skattebo can't play after being listed as questionable with a hamstring injury. Desrosiers has yet to play in a regular-season game this season. In three preseason games, he rushed 23 times for 166 yards and a touchdown.
injuryReports.injury: Desrosiers could serve as a backup for the Giants on Sunday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Greg Newsome II
injuryReports.returnComment: Newsome is healthy again after missing the Week 7 win over the Texans due to a concussion. The 26-year-old signed a three-year extension with the team Tuesday and will resume his role as one of its starting cornerbacks during Sunday's matchup against the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Newsome (concussion) wasn't listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jevon Holland
injuryReports.returnComment: Holland was forced to miss the team's overtime win against the Texans in Week 7 while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to have cleared concussion protocol. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role in New York's secondary versus Philadelphia on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Holland (concussion) was not listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Theo Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson appears to be back to full health after missing the team's last two contests while nursing a neck injury. The 25-year-old will be back in his No. 2 role at tight end behind starter Isaiah Likely against the Eagles on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (neck) was a full participant at the Giants' practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Trevin Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Garrett Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Nahshon Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Joseph Ossai
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Mason Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Troy Reeder
injuryReports.returnComment: Reeder is returning to New York after having been released by the Jets in October. The 32-year-old has logged four tackles (one solo) across six outings this season and will likely continue to see the majority of his playing time come on special teams during his second tenure with the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: The Jets signed Reeder to their active roster Monday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Will McDonald IV
injuryReports.returnComment: The 2023 first-round pick racked up 18.5 sacks over the previous two seasons and has three on his ledger through nine games in 2026, but he's seen his playing time tail off with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick David Bailey and the addition of Kingsley Enagbare in free agency. Though McDonald is hopeful to land with a team that can present him with a clearer path to a full-time role, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that McDonald "is going to be here" once the deadline passes, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.
injuryReports.injury: McDonald put in a request for the Jets to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Ian Rapoport and Rich Cimini of ESPN report.

injuryReports.name: Jason Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders provided all the offense for New York in Week 9, making exactly four field goals for the second straight week and third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards before pulling his lone miss wide left from 53 yards, all of which came in the first half. Sanders has now gone 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Adonai Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Kenyon Sadiq
injuryReports.returnComment: After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.
injuryReports.injury: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooper worked as the clear No.1 receiver for the Jets in the absence of Garrett Wilson (concussion), leading the team in targets, catches and receiving yards while Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his seven targets. Prior to finishing without a target in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders, Cooper delivered consecutive performances with at least 103 yards and a touchdown, so he has been effective in three of four games since returning from an IR stint due to a Week 1 ankle injury. Even if Wilson returns in Week 10, Cooper looks likely to remain involved in what could be a pass-heavy game plan against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Cooper caught eight of 11 targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Geno Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards.

injuryReports.name: Braelon Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Breece Hall
injuryReports.returnComment: Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.
injuryReports.injury: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: VJ Payne
injuryReports.returnComment: Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Dane Belton
injuryReports.returnComment: Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Belton recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo) and a pass defensed in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jamien Sherwood
injuryReports.returnComment: Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Sherwood recorded 14 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: David Bailey
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing Week 8 with the groin injury he suffered the previous week, Bailey appears poised to return after missing just one contest. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Bailey has piled up 35 tackles (21 solo), including 5.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.
injuryReports.injury: Bailey (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Max Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: In a corresponding transaction, the Jets signed tackle Blake Freeland to their active roster. Mitchell, who has not made a start on the offensive line yet this season, will now have to miss at least the next four games.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams ran a total of one route on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks against Las Vegas, but he made it count with a red-zone touchdown. The Jets' fourth receiver behind Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, Williams has no fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's date with the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Williams caught an 18-yard touchdown on his lone target in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Ben Skowronek
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Doneiko Slaughter
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Brandin Echols
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Chris Boswell
injuryReports.returnComment: Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Boswell made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Pittman has missed the Steelers' last four games and is now eligible to be activated from IR at any point, but based on the receiver's comments, he doesn't appear to be trending toward a return to action following the team's Week 9 bye. The wideout noted that his left foot injury that first cropped up following the season opener was originally plantar fasciitis but has since "morphed into something else." While it's encouraging that he's at least healthy enough to start running again, Pittman didn't indicate when he might be ready to resume practicing with the team.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Germie Bernard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Pat Freiermuth
injuryReports.returnComment: With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.
injuryReports.injury: Freiermuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. He added one rushing attempt for a one-yard touchdown.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Rico Dowdle
injuryReports.returnComment: Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: DK Metcalf
injuryReports.returnComment: Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Rodgers
injuryReports.returnComment: Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Rodgers completed 13 of 25 passes for 172 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Warren
injuryReports.returnComment: Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: The Steelers signed Smith off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Payton Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson totaled six tackles (three solo) and an interception during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Patrick Queen
injuryReports.returnComment: Queen had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles in addition to registering his first sack of the campaign. The 2020 first-round pick has now logged 48 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across seven games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Queen compiled 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Gracen Halton
injuryReports.returnComment: ir
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Mac Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders prior to the deadline.
injuryReports.injury: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries in Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.

injuryReports.name: Mike Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jordan James
